t: Serers believe in a supreme deity, Roog, and address their prayers to the pangool, the ancestral spirits and saints, who are held to carry the prayers of the living to the Divine.
Each Serer family has a totem, the tiim, which is both a prohibition and a guardian: the totem of the Joof family is the antelope, of the Njie the lion, of the Sène the hare.
At the Xooy ceremony the initiated Saltigue, the Serer high priests and priestesses, foretell the coming year before the community at Fatick, in the first week of June.
dyk: Serer spirituality rejects the notion of heaven and hell: a soul accepted by the ancestors may enter Jaaniiw, the place where good souls go, and return to earth through reincarnation, while a rejected soul wanders.
ev: Serers refuse the Muslim leader War Jabi's forced conversion and Sharia law, are defeated, and the first Serer exodus from Tekrur follows
Lamane Jegan Joof founds the village of Tukar, where the Raan festival is held each April; Serers begin to move south from the Senegal River valley
In the Islamic marabout wars, Serers at Naodorou, Kaymor and Ngaye kill themselves rather than be conquered, some jumping into the Well of Tahompa
The Serers are a target of the jihad led by the Mandinka cleric Ma Ba Jaxoo
The Serer king of Sine, Kumba Ndoffene Famak Joof, defeats and kills Maba Diakhou Bâ at the Battle of Fandane-Thiouthioune
French colonial forces conquer Senegal, ending the inter-ethnic wars involving the Serer; conversion to Islam then accelerates
The funeral rites of the Serer kings are last performed after the death of Maad a Sinig Mahecor Joof, the last king of Sine

f.origin: Senegambia in West Africa, among the Serer people, whose ancestors moved south from the Senegal River valley from around the 11th century, with the old Serer kingdom of Sine at its centre; the village of Tukar was founded by Lamane Jegan Joof around the 11th century.
f.founder: none: the religion is the Serer people's original religion; the founders of Serer villages, the lamane, are remembered as accompanied by the pangool and as the first priests and custodians of the shrines.
f.scriptures: none written: ancient chants and poems, myths and teachings handed down by Serer priests and elders, including the Serer creation myth.
f.followers: Most Serers converted to Islam and Christianity after colonisation (about 85% of the Serer people were Muslim by the 1990s), but many still follow the Serer religion, especially in the ancient Kingdom of Sine.
